The most comprehensive federal program is that administered by the Department of Housing and Urban Development "Comprehensive Planning Assistance," (Housing Act of 1954, Sec. 201 as amended, Public Law 83-560, 68. Stat. 590, 640; 40 U.S.C. 461.) commonly called the 701 Program. This program provides grants for a broad range of planning projects, including the development of administrative and technical capabilities; to build or strengthen governmental institutions and area wide structures that address and respond to community development issues; and to improve inter-governmental planning and coordination. This program is supplemented by the Technical Assistance Act of HUD (Department of Housing and Urban Development Act of 1965, sec. 3)B; Public Law 89-174, 79 Stat. 667; 42 U.S.C. 3531.) which provides a base of advisory services and counsels as well as supporting program planning and providing financing advice.
In addition to this, the BIA, in discharging its trust responsibility to Indian tribes, may provide various types of resources to assist the Crow tribe in both its comprehensive reservation and community planning as well as for specific development projects.
Other federal agencies provide planning assistance but these will be discussed under the specific programs and services which will be impacted.
The State of Montana, through their Department of Community Affairs, also makes available a wide range of planning assistance to counties and municipalities and acts in a coordinating role between these levels and the federal government. Various other state agencies such as Health and Education have provided planning assistance in related programs for many decades.
